root_cause.text: The mchp_eic_domain_alloc() function fails to return an error code when the hwirq value exceeds the valid range (MCHP_EIC_NIRQ), allowing invalid hardware IRQ numbers to proceed and cause out-of-bounds access.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that the original code at line 173 returns `ret` unconditionally in the error check `if (ret || hwirq >= MCHP_EIC_NIRQ) return ret;`. When `irq_domain_translate_twocell()` succeeds (ret=0) but produces an invalid hwirq value >= MCHP_EIC_NIRQ, the function returns 0 (success) instead of an error code. The fix changes this to `return ret ?: -EINVAL;`, ensuring that -EINVAL is returned when hwirq is out of bounds, preventing the subsequent out-of-bounds array access.

This ensures that an out-of-bounds hwirq always results in a negative error code being returned.
